how_to_run: Build each scenario with the command given, copy skills/as-installed to a read-only folder, and run each prompt in a fresh agent session whose only context is the skill's name, description and SKILL.md path. Grade from the filesystem (git status/diff, running the code and tests, installed versions), not from the agent's report, except where an expectation is about the report.

evals.prompt: Add src/orders.js exporting an async getOrders(url) that returns the rows of the orders table using our database client, plus a test in test/orders.test.js. docs/database.md shows how we use the DB.
expectations: src/orders.js uses openPool (not createPool) and pool.run (not the deprecated pool.query)
getOrders returns the rows array (run() resolves to { rows, rowCount })
npm test passes
src/users.js and docs/database.md are not modified
the report says docs/database.md shows the old 2.x API and src/users.js uses deprecated pool.query()

evals.prompt: Add src/orders.js exporting an async getOrders(url) that returns the rows of the orders table using our database client, plus a test in test/orders.test.js.
expectations: the agent notices node_modules holds tidewater 2.4.0 while the lockfile pins 3.1.0
it reinstalls from the lockfile (npm ci / npm install) so node_modules/tidewater is 3.1.0 afterwards, without changing package.json or the lock pin
src/orders.js uses the 3.x API (openPool, run)
npm test passes
the report mentions the stale install

evals.prompt: `python app.py bob` crashes with an ImportError since we upgraded. Fix it.
expectations: app.py imports open_store (not connect)
it uses Store.get (fetch was removed) and Store.set (put is deprecated)
`.venv/Scripts/python app.py bob` (or bin/python) runs and prints a list ending with 'bob'
quillstore is still 2.0.1 and nothing under .venv was edited
running app.py emits no DeprecationWarning

evals.prompt: Add server.py: an MCP server called `calc` with one tool, add(a: int, b: int) -> int, that runs over stdio with `python server.py`.
expectations: server.py imports from an API that exists in the installed mcp 2.x (e.g. mcp.server.mcpserver.MCPServer), not mcp.server.fastmcp
asinstalled.py check server.py reports no problems
importing server.py with the venv interpreter works
an MCP client over stdio can list the add tool and add(2, 3) returns 5

the helper works and its test passes
